html:
SMTO-TSK-0020 — This task can't be paused or resumed right now

GUID: 495f5275-03be-4b11-85cf-8c4351d89c77
Slug: pause-state-invalid
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Pause or Resume you chose doesn't fit what the task is doing now. For example, it may have already finished, already continued, or not be paused. SMTO left the task as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and look at the task's latest reply to see whether it is running, Paused, waiting for you, or finished. The task's state may have changed since the button was shown, which is why it was refused.
  2. Use the button the task offers now: Pause after current action while it runs, or Resume when it shows Paused. Each button only works in the state it is shown for.
  3. If the task already finished, send a new message to continue the work instead. A finished task can't be paused or resumed, but a new message starts the next step.

What success looks like

  • The task shows Paused after you pause it, or starts working again after you resume it.

If it still fails

  • If Resume keeps failing on a paused task, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the task's saved pause information may be damaged. Don't delete the conversation to fix it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Pause or resume validation found the run in a status the control does not allow (not pausable, not paused for manual continuation, already continued) or a saved resume destination that is not a valid resume state.

What this means

  • Pause/resume validation finds a source or restored destination status outside the control's permitted states. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Pause/resume validation finds a source or restored destination status outside the control's permitted states.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current status, manual-pause state and the resume destination recorded by the owner.

How to fix it

  • Read the run's current status: Pause requires a resumable state; manual continuation requires paused, paused_budget, partial, waiting_user or blocked with no existing continuation; the saved manual_pause.resume_status must be a valid resume state. Refresh and use only the control the current state offers. An invalid saved destination indicates damaged run state; capture the details rather than editing it.
  • Refresh the run’s current controls. Use Pause or Continue only when offered for its authoritative state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended control is offered and accepted for the authoritative current state.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
